title: Zero Polynomial Testing in Bounded Error Polynomial Time
statement: The language of encodings of well-formed algebraic circuits over the integer polynomials that compute the zero polynomial has a randomized polynomial-time decision procedure: it halts within a polynomial bound on every choice sequence and outputs the correct membership bit with probability at least $2/3$ on every input.
hypotheses_covered: Input belongs to the zero-polynomial language, defined by well-formed encoded algebraic circuits over the integers computing the zero polynomial
Polynomial-time bound of the form c(n^d+1) for natural-number constants c and d
Halts within the time bound on every branch
Correct membership-bit output with probability at least 2/3 on every input
